abstract: Short Fibre Reinforced Polypropylene (FRP) electrets exhibit much higher Thermally Stimulated Depolarization Current (TSDC) as compared to isotropic polypropylene. Uniaxial stretched polypropylene (SPP) on the other hand, shows lower polarization in comparison to the isotropic sheet and a shift towards higher temperatures in two TSDC peaks observed between 60 and 150/spl deg/C. This is despite the observation that stretched polypropylene reinforces the structure and improves the toughness and strength in the direction of stretching. The low TSDC in SPP is attributed to reduced segmental mobility. This interpretation is analyzed further and it is suggested that further work on measurement of charge distribution profiles is essential in SPP and FRP to understand the polarization mechanism and take up development of devices such as electret filters.

articleTitle: The study of the open-circuit thermally stimulated discharge on the guest-host nonlinear optical polymer electret DR1/PMMA film
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In this paper the charge dynamic characteristic of the guest-host NLO polymer electret DR1/PMMA films after corona poling is investigated by means of the thermally stimulated discharge (TSD) technology. The results indicate that in the sample poled by the constant voltage corona charging near the glass transition temperature (Tg) there are two kinds of charges: space charge trapped by the traps of sample and dipole charge originating from the oriented dipole, and the dipole charge is completely compensated by the space charge. Most of trap energy levels of the space charges are higher than the bound levels of dipole charges at the suitable poling temperature. The breadth B of site distribution in the KWW stretched exponential expression applied to fit the relaxation of the oriented dipole is correlated to the interaction between dipole and space charge. Aging can lead to the space charge transferring to deeper traps due to the fast retrapping effect, which makes the space charge more stable, and consequently improves the orientation stability of the dipole and optical nonlinear stability.

articleTitle: Mechanisms of thermoluminescence peaks emergence in PVDF in the temperature range 80-380 K
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In the spectra of thermally stimulated luminescence of PVDF the authors observed two relaxation peaks in the low-temperature region: the /spl gamma/-peak at 120 K and the /spl beta/-peak at 190 K, the relative value of which correlates to the degree of the sample crystallinity. Molecular movement in amorphous and crystalline regions of PVDF explains their origin, correspondingly. In the region of 320 K in the TL spectra they observed the /spl alpha/-peak. It also shows on the thermally stimulated depolarization curve of PVDF, and is due to electronic processes.

articleTitle: Photonic gaps and localization of light in composite materials
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The author provides an overview of the development of ideas leading to the postulation of photonic gaps in composite materials. He looks at the role of defects and the structure of composite materials, the optimum conditions for gap formation and the fabrication of photonic band gap materials. Finally, future prospects for this field are briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Photoinduced anisotropy in chalcogenide glasses
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: A model is formulated that allows one to explain some basic characteristic features of photoinduced anisotropy in glassy semiconductors. The model assumes the occurrence of correlated pairs of localized states for electrons and holes and relates photoinduced anisotropy to generation of geminate electron-hole pairs trapped by these localized states.

articleTitle: Photocapacitance and photoreflectance characterization of Pb/sub 3/O/sub 4/ photoelectrets
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: High resistivity with density of deep traps in Pb/sub 3/O/sub 4/ layers is suitable for photoelectret applications. Recently the Pb/sub 3/O/sub 4/ physical characterization was found to be of interest due to anomalies of structural and electrical properties. Photocapacitance (PC) spectra, that is, dependence of photoresponses /spl Delta/C(/spl lambda/), where /spl lambda/ - the wavelength of falling irradiation, allow to expressively evaluate the width of the forbidden band E/sub g/. Besides, the investigation of the PC effect, as it is experimentally Shown, can resolve a thin structure of energy bands. Samples for such measurements should be rather high-resistant (/spl rho//spl ges/ 10/sup 3/...10/sup 4/ Ohm.cm) and photosensitive. Polycrystalline layers of the Pb/sub 3/O/sub 4/ meet these requirements completely. One of the promising non-contact optical methods of studying band structure is the modulation of photoreflectance (PR). Despite of smaller sensitivity of PR (minimal changes of reflectance /spl Delta/R/R=10/sup 4/) in comparison, for example, with electroreflectance, the indicated method allows to determine the change of concentration and the time of their relaxation. We initiated the study with expectation of finding particular characteristics in PR lineshapes, which are related to the local states structure in the forbidden band of the Pb3O/sub 4/ photoelectret layers.

articleTitle: The dielectrical properties of steroidal glycosides corresponding to saponins class and their interaction with bovine albumin
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Molecules of steroidal glycosides (SG) possess a polar, asymetric, stretched, amphiphilic structure. We proposed that crystallic fine films of SG will have unique properties as an optical active dielectric. As infinite homogeneous anisotropal dielectrical environment the crystallic films of SG in different directions will have a different means of refractive index and dielectrical penetrability, which can be determined by solving the inverse ellipsometric problem. In our investigations we used the ellipsometric multiangle measurements of polarization angles using the method of four-zones for thin films of SG and their aglycones and used the soft ionization of 252-Cf Time-of-Flight Plasma Desorption Mass Spectrometry (PDMS) for SG characterization and structural confirmation.

articleTitle: Interfacial interactions in silica gel-PMMA composite materials
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The dense inorganic-organic composite used in the present investigation involves the widely used macromolecular phase, poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA), in-situ polymerized into the porous silica-gel matrix. The materials were studied by means of the thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC) dielectric technique, applied in the extended temperature range -260 to +170 /spl deg/C, which covers the relaxation response in the entire glassy region of the dielectrically active polymeric component. Earlier reports on similar composites based on the sol-gel process are mainly concentrated on aspects of their mechanical, thermal and optical response.

articleTitle: A model of long time decay of space charge in polymers
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The basic processes determining the time evolution of current carriers allow one to predict the observed phenomenon of a very slow decay of implanted charge. According to the model presented here, the charge decay takes place in two distinct stages: the first is rapid but the second slow and linear, whereas the conductivity evolution takes place in three stages. In the first stage one observes a sudden decrease of conductivity; in the second its slow recovery, and in the third stage, when the source of electric field no longer exists, one observes more rapid, close to exponential, return to the equilibrium value.

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated depolarization current of BaTiO/sub 3//P[VDF(70)-TrFE(30)] 0-3 ferroelectric composites
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: 0-3 ferroelectric composites of barium titanate (BT) and vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene copolymer P[VDF(70)-TrFE(30)] with different volume fraction of BT were prepared by solution blending followed by compression-molding. The thermally stimulated depolarization current (TSDC) of the composites has been measured. Three detrapping charge and two phase transition peaks (one for copolymer and another for ceramic) are observed in TSDC spectra above room temperature. For the composite sample in which only the ceramic phase is polarized, the detrapping charge peaks disappeared, which indicates that the TSDC originates from the copolymer phase. According to the analysis of phase transition, the structural origin of TSDC peaks is proposed. The detrapping charge density increases as increasing BT content, which shows that ceramic inclusions enhance the ability of charge storage in the composites.

articleTitle: Dielectric properties of polystyrene doped with DR1 guest molecules
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: It has been shown that presence of DR1 molecules affects the /spl alpha/ relaxation behaviour of a host polymer in such a way that the distribution of relaxation times becomes wider, the dielectric constant and the dielectric strength increase, while the dopant shows a definite plasticizing effect. It has been found that the PS/DR1 system is not a thermoreologically simple one. It is probable therefore that the /spl beta/ processes in polystyrene influence relaxation behavior of the chromophore molecules at sub-T/sub g/ temperatures.

articleTitle: Anionic collagen for biomedical application
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In this work we describe the physicochemical and rheological properties and the biological behavior (biocompatibility and tissue supporting ability of anionic collagen based biomaterials intended for tissue reconstruction.

articleTitle: The structural analysis of miscible polymer blends using thermally stimulated depolarization current method
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In this study, we measured the thermally stimulated depolarization current (TSDC) spectra of the glass transition of poly(vinyl methyl ether)/polystyrene (PVME/PS) blends, and discussed the homogeneity of the blend structure in a single-phase state comparing with the results of transmission electron microscopy (TEM) photographs.

articleTitle: The determination of spatial distribution of polarization in electro-active ceramic/polymer composite sensors using the laser intensity modulation method (LIMM)
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Reports the results of a determination of the spatial distribution of the polarization in composite sensors of ferroelectric calcium modified lead titanate (PTCa) and the copolymer of vinylidene fluoride with trifluoroethylene, P(VDF-TrFE) using a laser intensity modulation method (LIMM).

articleTitle: Space charge measurements in ionomer films exposed by corona discharge
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Ionomers are thermoplastic polymers functionalized by metal ionic groups attached to backbone chains of the host polymers. The ion groups form clusters and crosslink the backbone chains. In contrast to the ordinary covalent bond structure, for crosslinkage with ions, the bond energy decreases at high temperature. Ionomers, therefore, retain thermoplastic properties, although the function of the ionic clusters has not been theoretically explained. The adhesion strength and miscibility of host polymers are also improved by the ionic radicals. Among many kinds of host polymers, ethylene methacrylic acid copolymer is the most common base resin for manufacturing ethylene ionomers. Ethylene ionomers are used in skin packaging technology, such as polymer laminated papers and aluminum coated polymer films. It has been recently found that an ethylene ionomer can store charges after corona discharge exposure from surface potential measurements. As a part of plasma chemistry, the effect of corona discharge on polymers is usually restricted to analysing surface properties. The pulsed electroacoustic (PEA) method was used to measure space charge distributions through the thickness of ethylene ionomer specimens which include Mg or Al ions.

articleTitle: Application of thermally stimulated currents method to study of the special glasses structure
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Thermally stimulated current (thermally stimulated polarisation, TSPC, and thermally stimulated depolarisation, TSDC) method has been used to investigate the charge motion and trap levels in crystalline dielectrics and semiconductors. Recently this technique has been also used to study alkali motion in glasses. In earlier papers we have shown that the TSPC/TSDC experiments could be applied for determination of changes of silicate glasses structure. In this paper the results of measurements of thermally stimulated currents of special glasses are presented. The subjects of investigation were photochromic, ionic conducting and porous glasses.

articleTitle: Dielectric and spectral characteristics of some aromatic polyether films and tablets
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The authors study a series of polyethers and polyesters based on chloromethyl oxetane embedded in polymer matrices of polymethyl metacrylate (PMMA) and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) type. These polymers have been studied both in solid state as thin films deposed on quartz disks and in solution. The electronic absorption spectra and photochromic effects in such materials are discussed and the polarisation current density is measured.

articleTitle: The use of various ionenes as humidity sensors
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The ionene sensors with low x and y values are of low molecular weight and are poor film forming materials. We have shown that the ionenes with x=6 and y=10 are most suitable as humidity sensing materials. Attempts with the use of N/sup +/ ionenes with TCNQ salts are discussed showing that at specific concentration of TCNQ these sensors can be used as current limiting elements in the system and/or their indicators.

articleTitle: Characterization and dielectric properties of new semi-interpenetrating polymer networks
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: New semi-interpenetrating polymer networks (semi-IPNs) were prepared on the basis of linear polyurethane (LPU) and trimerized dicyanic ether of bisphenol-A crosslinked (TDCE). Their structural properties were investigated by wide-angle and small-angle X-ray spectroscopy (WAXS and SAXS). The dynamic dielectric properties were measured by thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC) techniques and broadband dielectric relaxation spectroscopy (DRS). All techniques provide strong evidence for homogeneous structure without any indication of microphase separation.

articleTitle: Dielectric relaxation and polarisation phenomena in poly(methyl metracrylate) with the disperse red 1 dye
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In this work the poling process of the NLO guest-host system consisting of poly(methyl metacrylate): PMMA, and disperse red 1, DR1, is investigated with the purpose of getting information about the poling process and then optimize it. Measurements of pyroelectric activity of the poled samples are employed to evaluate the efficiency of the process since its value is directly proportional to the electric polarisation in the sample. Here, the poling was performed using the corona triode with constant current allowing one to measure the sample voltage during charging and parameters such as the temperature, electric field and poling time were varied. It is also shown that the electric conduction and also the dielectric constant can be obtained from the potential build-up curves.

articleTitle: Dielectric study of miscibility in poly(methyl acrylate)-poly(methyl methacrylate) sequential interpenetrating polymer networks
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The miscibility of PMA/PMMA interpenetrating polymer networks (IPNs) is studied as a function of the crosslinking density using dielectric and dynamic-mechanical techniques.
