articleTitle: Photoinduced discharge of SiO/sub 2/ electret film. II. Theory
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Photodepopulation spectroscopy is a traditional tool to study electronic localized states in SiO/sub 2/ and Si based metal-oxide-semiconductor devices especially at the Si-SiO/sub 2/ interface. Normally, this study reveals the occurrence of electron acceptor-like traps with the energy of around 3 eV below the SiO/sub 2/ conduction band. Higher photocurrent and faster photoinduced discharge with decreasing wavelength of inducing light is attributed to increasing photoionization cross section with increasing photon energy. However, both the photocurrent and photoinduced discharge do not reveal a sharp edge effect at the photon energy hv equal to the photoionization energy although the photocurrent is much weaker and the discharge is much slower at hv<3 eV. It is also worth noting that the experimentally observed kinetics of photoinduced discharge becomes strongly non-exponential at such low photon energies implying deviation from a simple single-photon excitation process. One should also bear in mind that, in addition to deep traps, a high density of shallower band-tail states must occur near a semiconductor disordered dielectric interface. In the present work we formulate an alternative model describing photoinduced discharge of SiO/sub 2/ electret films. The model considers carrier photoionization as a two-step process. On the first step a carrier makes a photon-assisted tunneling jump from a deep trap into a bandtail state, Being localized in this state for a sufficiently long time the carrier may pick up an energy from a second photon that could allow it to be released into extended states in the bulk of the SiO/sub 2/ film.

articleTitle: Dielectric and mechanical behaviour of ordered polyurethane networks based on mesogenic diol
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In this work we have studied the effect of ordered structure of polyurethane LCNs, based on poly(oxypropylene)triol (T), 2(4)-methyl-1,3-phenylene diisocyanate (Dr) and the mesogenic diol (D) cured at isotropic state, on the dielectric and dynamic mechanical behaviour. As was shown previously for uncrosslinked polymer from D and DI by DSC, X-ray scattering and polarizing microscopy, a nematic phase forms on cooling and freezes into the LC glassy state. On heating, the mesophase melts and, subsequently, a better-ordered smectic phase is formed at 110 /spl deg/C, melting at 130/spl deg/C.

articleTitle: Electret properties of PETP containing ferrocene units
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PETP) containing ferrocene units in the main chain is expected to give a polymer with new electrical properties. It is well known that ferrocene units incorporated into a polymer backbone can enhance its weatherability and stabilize the polymer against the degrading effects of light. Some ferrocene compounds are known to be UV light absorbers. It is not known how the modification of PETP affects the charge storage in polymeric samples. The purpose of this work is the study of the electret properties of PETP containing ferrocene units.

articleTitle: Influence of boron ion implantation on the mechanics and electret properties of Si/sub 3/N/sub 4/ single layer film
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Amorphous silicon nitride (Si/sub 3/N/sub 4/) film has outstanding electret properties and it is compatible with micromachining technology. Therefore, it is expected to be used as an electret vibrating membrane in miniature microphones. One of the most important parameters of characterizing electret-vibrating membranes is flexibility. So the reduction of internal stress due to boron ion implantation for the LPCVD Si/sub 3/N/sub 4/ film on silicon substrate is discussed first. The charge storage ability for the Si/sub 3/N/sub 4/ films B+ implanted by various doses and energies are investigated by means of negative corona charging, the isothermal surface potential decay measurements and open-circuit thermally stimulated discharge (TSD) current spectrum analysis.

articleTitle: Effects of electric conduction on electrical response of electrorheological fluids
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In the present study, the current-voltage characteristics and the electrical responses of the electrorheological (ER) fluids were measured under DC electric field conditions. The test fluids consisted of microsphere particles with various moisture levels dispersed in a silicone oil. The current density/electric field curves could roughly be fitted with sinh functions suggesting ionic conduction. The forces of cohesion between individual particles in the ER fluids were also determined using a mathematical model. The current-force relationship predicted by the theory was compared to experimental results for the test fluids.

articleTitle: Comparative dielectric studies of segmental and normal mode dynamics of poly(oxybutylene) and poly(oxyethylene)-poly(oxybutylene) diblock copolymers
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Diblock copolymers of ethylene oxide (E) and 1,2-butylene oxide (B), E/sub 30/B/sub n/, with a constant E-block length of 30 units and various B-block lengths (n=3-30), were investigated, in parallel with a series of homopoly(oxybutylene)s of similar B-block lengths, using broadband dielectric relaxation spectroscopy (10/sup -2/ 10/sup 9/ Hz). The normal mode relaxation process due to reorientation of the end-to-end vector, as well as the main (segmental) process caused by local chain motions, exhibited by the B-blocks in the copolymers and respectively by the homopoly(oxybutylene), were studied in comparison with each other. The Rouse model has been found to describe satisfactorily the molecular mobility of B/sub n/ blocks in the copolymers, whereas deviations from that model have been observed for the homopolymers. The results show that the B-blocks in the copolymers, constrained between lamellar crystals created by E-blocks, exhibit slower large scale motions.

articleTitle: PZT/P(VDF-TrFE) nanocomposites for ultrasonic hydrophone application
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: 0-3 composites with nanosized lead zirconate titanate (PZT) powder imbedded in a vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene copolymer (P(VDF-TrFE)) matrix have been fabricated. Since the piezoelectric coefficients of PZT and P(VDF-TrFE) have opposite signs, the PZT and P(VDF-TrFE) phases in the nanocomposites were poled in opposite directions in order to enhance the piezoelectric activity. The PZT powder, prepared by a sol-gel process, has a tetragonal structure. The ratio of the [002] and [200] X-ray diffraction peaks was used as a measure of the degree of poling in the ceramic phase. The piezoelectric coefficient of the nanocomposite film was measured by a laser interferometry technique. A needle type hydrophone for the calibration of medical ultrasonic transducers was fabricated using the nanocomposite as the sensing element and its performance was evaluated.

articleTitle: Use of corona discharge for promoting polyaniline to the conductive state
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In this article we show the use of the corona discharge to dope thin layers of PANI coated on PET films. It is also shown that the neutral excited molecules generated inthe corona discharge are responsible for the doping process in PANI. It is believed that this novel technique could be employed in a continuous doping process aiming to produce films with large area for anti-electrostatic packing applications.

articleTitle: Polarizing mechanism of colloidal metal particles formation in polymer electrets
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Thermal treatment of polymers in electric fields induces changes in their structure and physico-mechanical properties. Noticeable variations are observed at considerable values of the field intensity (about hundreds of kV/cm), namely dipolar polarization of the polymer, increased number and dimensions of ordered areas. Modification of polymer structure under the applied electric field could be an outcome of not only dipolar polarization alone but also charge carrier injection from the electrodes. As for, for example, a gradual transfer of /spl alpha/-form into /spl beta/-form proceeds in polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) in the field of injected charge due to the bulk charge relaxation. The mentioned phenomena are most peculiar to metal-polymer electrets (MPE) formed by thermal treatment of polymers between electrodes of unlike metals. Polarization in MPE is accompanied by diffusion of atoms and ions of electrode metal into the polymer, being the process of mainly electrochemical nature. Charge injection can be intensified at low field voltage by increasing the actual contact area between the electrode and dielectric. The method makes it possible to control charge density and its distribution across electret thickness. Promising is the employment of liquid-metal electrodes aimed at increasing contact area between electrode and polarized polymer. In this case one is able to observe charge injection into the polymer together with metal diffusion from the electrode into the polymer layer bulk. This work aimed to investigate polarisation effect on metal diffusion and formation of colloidal metal particles in polymer electrets.

articleTitle: Electric-field dependence of photogeneration in charge-transfer complexes of polyparacyclophanes with 2,4,7-trinitrofluorenone
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In the present work the photoconductivity of two different polyparacyclophanes doped with 2,4,7-trinitrofluorenone (TNF) was investigated by means of surface potential discharge method. The photogeneration quantum yield is compared with the results for the poly(N-vinylcarbazole) (PVK) pure and doped with TNF and the field dependences of the photogeneration yield are analyzed using the Onsager and the Braun models.

articleTitle: Dielectric characteristic of a swelling gel
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Swelling gels are very attractive for applications in various domains:biomaterials, agriculture, security.... This study concerns a crosslinked. PolyAcrylAcid (P(AA)) synthesized by inverse suspension polymerization. The principal chemical property of this material is related to acrylate groups which are able to absorb an important amount of liquid. The swelling property of crosslinked P(AA) are dependent upon different parameters such as temperature, solution pH, crosslinking ratio. Surprisingly, the molecular mechanism of swelling remains unclear. The aim of this work is to analyze molecular mobility of crosslinked P(AA) by Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) and Thermally Stimulated Current (TSC). The influence of heptane has been followed in order to established the molecular origin of the various events.

articleTitle: Construction of a series of electrification of atomic groups by measuring frictional electrification between Langmuir-Blodgett films
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In the present work, a new type of apparatus for measuring frictional electrification between flat surfaces was constructed and the frictional electrification between LB films and between polymer films was investigated. From the results a series of frictional electrification studies of atomic groups was proposed.

articleTitle: Dielectric spectra of a partially fluorinated chromophore/amorphous teflon AF guest-host system
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: A new guest-host polymer was prepared from amorphous teflon AF and an azomethine dye and investigated by dielectric spectroscopy. The spectra show a relaxation with an activation energy of 0.71 eV which is attributed to the chromophore and which can be described with a Cole-Cole function.

articleTitle: Electrical and dielectric properties of new polyurethane ionomers
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Ionomers are polymers which contain charge groups in their molecular structure. Here we report the electrical and dielectric properties of new polyurethane ionomers based on poly(ethylene oxide) with nonionic hard segments of varying length and flexible segments containing alkali ions (Li/sup +/, Na/sup +/, K/sup +/) or protons (H*) by means of TSDC-DRS. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) were employed for structural investigation. The combined results by the different techniques indicate the coexistence of two morphologies: the microphase-separated structure characteristic of polyurethanes (hard-segment-rich microdomains in a soft-segment-rich matrix) and ionic aggregates (multiplets and clusters). Crystallization is observed at low hard segment contents(melting at about 305 K): the tendency for crystallization increasing upon hard segment extension and decreasing upon neutralization. Values of ionic conductivity are in the range of 10/sup -4/ S/m at 323 K, the conductivity in the amorphous polyurethanes being governed by the motion of the polymeric chains.

articleTitle: Field effect on the variable range hopping in amorphous materials
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: We develop an analytical model describing the field effect on the dark conductivity in positionally and energetically random hopping systems at finite temperatures. It is shown that under these conditions the conductivity obeys Mott's law provided the conventional temperature is replaced by an effective field-dependent temperature.

articleTitle: On the time variation of the electrical conductivity in some spinel magnetic ceramics
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In a previous paper we have reported on the time modification of the electrical conductivity /spl sigma/ of freshly prepared and quenched polycrystals of various spinel ferrites, observed at room temperature and above. We found that for some ferrites /spl sigma/ decreases whereas for others it increases, immediately after sintering. We assumed that this time effect (named by us "electric relaxation") can be explained by the probable changes in cation distribution between tetrahedral (A) and octahedral (B) sites of the spinel lattice which take place after rapidly cooling samples to reach the equilibrium distribution. The aim of the present paper is to report on the measurements of the time variation of the electrical conductivity on various polycrystalline ferrites to elucidate the complexity of the phenomenon.

articleTitle: Study of dielectric relaxations in polyamide 11 by thermostimulated currents and broadband dielectric spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The aim of this work is to investigate relaxation processes in various samples of polyamide 11: nonferroelectric samples and poled ferroelectric samples. Also, polyamide 11 samples with different levels of hydration were investigated.

articleTitle: Glass transition of one-dimensional chains of pNA molecules confined in AlPO/sub 4/-5 nanopores revealed by dielectric and pyroelectric spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In the present paper the authors describe results from (dynamic) pyroelectric experiments on the p-nitroaniline molecule confined in AlPO/sub 4/-5 nanopores, which allow a study of individual crystals. A comparison between dielectric and pyroelectric relaxation times is made.

articleTitle: Electret analysis of electronic properties of sillenite crystals
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The electron-electret state (EES) and photoelectret state (PES) of face doped sillenite crystals are investigated. the spatial distribution of an electrical field, potential and volumetric charge density are obtained. The influence of photoactive radiation on processes of formation and relaxation of electret states is investigated.

articleTitle: Average particle size in polymer blends obtained by dielectric spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Previously we focussed on the dielectric properties of laminates and blends consisting of a weakly conducting and an insulating phase. Dielectric spectroscopy was used as a tool to obtain information about the dimensions of the conducting phase. With decreasing thickness of the conducting layer in the laminates, the permittivities measured were found to deviate more and more from those predicted by the conventional, series mixture rule. This discrepancy allowed us to calculate the thickness of the ionic charge layer (or the Debye length) in the conducting phase and also the thickness of this phase itself, using a model derived by Trukhan. His mixture model incorporates not only conduction, but also diffusion of charges. DS was also performed on a blend of Vectra B particles in a polypropylene matrix. After deriving a new model, which combined Trukhan's model with Bottcher's equation for dielectric mixtures, we could calculate the average particle size. Here we will discuss which average particle size is actually determined by dielectric measurements.

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated depolarization currents investigations of relaxations in polyesters and copolyesters. I. /spl beta/ relaxations
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In this work new results on /spl beta/-relaxations for thermoplastic polyesters are presented to characterize the influence of the chemical structure on the motions which are at the origin of the TSDC relaxations.

articleTitle: Specific heat of solid dielectrics charged at room temperature
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: It is now recognized that the internal energy of insulating materials is greatly affected by the presence of trapped charges. In particular this feature was recently analysed from Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) measurements on polymers charged with the electron beam of a SEM. Trapped charges injected at room temperature produce a structural transformation in their immediate surrounding and a strong polarization of the whole sample. To complete this study the behaviour of the heat capacity of the material is investigated, after the injection of electrons, by studying its time evolution at room temperature. The results concern low density polyethylene after implantation of 30 keV energy electrons at variable dose corresponding to n trapped charges.

articleTitle: The dependence of the dielectric behaviour of rocks on the water content
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Natural polycrystalline granite and marble were studied by broadband dielectric relaxation spectroscopy (10/sup -2/-10/sup 6/ Hz) at room temperature and several water contents (pure water) of the specimens. The results show a dramatic dependence of the complex dielectric permittivity on the water content of the specimens even for very low hydration levels.

articleTitle: Polarization phenomena of aortic tissues: influence of biochemical extractions on the protein dynamic
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Cardiovascular tissues are complex materials primarily composed of structural proteins: collagen, elastin and glycoproteins. Nowadays, they are widely studied for the understanding of vascular pathologies, such as atherosclerosis, and for the conceiving of durable bioprostheses. If the collagen structure is well characterized, few researches have been performed on the thermoelectric properties of these two fibrous proteins. In this work we propose to examine the dielectric response of elastin and collagen in aortic tissues and to follow their evolution upon biochemical treatments.

articleTitle: Dielectric studies of glass transition in confined oligomers of propylene glycol
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: We report the results of the detailed studies of confinement on the glass transition of propylene glycol (PG) and its oligomers (PPGs). The molecular weight (MW) of the oligomers was 400, 1200 and 2000. Vycor glass (VG), characterized by a narrow distribution of pore diameters around 4.0 nm, was used for confinement. Both native and chemically treated glasses to render the inner pore surfaces hydrophobic were used. The techniques employed include thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC) and broadband dielectric relaxation spectroscopy (DRS). Compared to bulk liquids, confinement was found to cause a shift of the /spl alpha/ relaxation, associated with the glass transition, to higher frequencies/lower temperatures and a broadening of the response. Cooperativity effects are thought to be responsible for these changes.

articleTitle: On the energy spectrum of electrically active defects in polyethylene terephthalate (PET) films
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The TSD curves in PET films show two maxima: in the 80/spl deg/C region (/spl alpha/-peak) and at 125/spl deg/C (/spl beta/-peak). From the thermally stimulated depolarization results in PET films the quasi-two-dimensional electrically active defect (EAD) distribution function is reconstructed, The distribution function maximum for the /spl alpha/-peak shifts to the region of lower values during the PET films depolarization in the ambient air at a pressure of 1100 mbar as compared to measurements in vacuum.

articleTitle: TSC measurements on electrophotographic toner layers with charge control agent
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The tribocharge of toners is a major factor in the electrophotographic process, and CCAs (charge control agents) are used for toners to improve their tribocharging characteristics. However the tribocharging mechanism of toners with CCA has not sufficiently been clarified yet. We have been measuring thermally stimulated currents (TSC) on toner layers to study the tribocharging characteristics of polymers containing CCA. This paper describes the results of TSC measurements on a resin, CCA and resins containing CCA, and discusses charge trapping sites in resins with CCA.

articleTitle: TSDC and TSDC-TS study of segment mobility peculiarities in the phases of finely dispersed binary polymer blends
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: This work presents the results of investigation of segmental mobility in the set of polymer binary blends (poly(butylene terephthalate) (PET)/polycarbonate (PC), polyamid-6 (PA6)/acrylnitril-butadien-styren (ABS) and polyolefin blends). The study was carried out by means of the thermally stimulated depolarization currents method (TSD). The data concerning the blend phase morphology and thermodynamic compatibility of the blend components were used for interpretation of the results.

articleTitle: Do the piezoelectric, pyroelectric and ferroelectric properties of biological materials have any physiological significance?
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Many thousands of papers have been published on the piezoelectric, pyroelectric and ferroelectric properties of single crystals, ceramics, polymers and liquid crystals. Yet fewer than 100 papers have appeared on these properties in biological materials. Piezoelectric and pyroelectric effects have been measured in a number of plant and animal tissues and the possible existence of ferroelectricity has also been suggested. This paper will review some measurements and speculate on their significance. Specific examples will include piezoelectricity in a crystalline material in the pineal gland of the brain, pyroelectricity in the heat sensing organs of certain varieties of snakes and beetles, and ferroelectricity in the conduction of action potentials in nerve and muscle cells.

articleTitle: Dielectric spectroscopy analysis of electrically aged low density polyethylene
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The analysis of the low frequency dielectric loss of electrically aged LDPE shows an increase with electrical ageing. This could be further verified by extending the frequency range down to 10-5 Hz in order to measure the changes at the expected peak maximum. TSDC results are however inconclusive whether the measured current is due to dipoles or space charge. The observed difference between charge release from the two samples surfaces indicates that there is an asymmetrical distribution of space charge or polarization. This agrees with the optical microscope observations showing that one of the sides has a greater water tree density than the other. A difference on the initial TSDC current level (near 20/spl deg/C) appears to be more dependent on the short-circuit time than on the poling time. If a TSDC is performed without poling the measured current is near zero, revealing that space charges have been removed or that the dipoles have been disoriented.

articleTitle: Thermal treatment effects on phase transitions in P(VDF-TrFE)
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The authors present DSC studies where heating and cooling rates and also thermal treatments were varied systematically. The results for 60/40 P(VDFTrFE) are presented in this paper which confirm the importance of thermal history and also show that samples with various configurations in terms of ferroelectric phases can be obtained in a somewhat controlled way via thermal treatment.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo simulation of trapping and recombination kinetics of charge carriers' in one-dimensional structures
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In this paper a new Monte Carlo method is described for the calculation of trapping and recombination kinetics in one-dimensional systems. Using the model it is possible to study the effect of charge carrier transport on trapping kinetics.

articleTitle: LIMM investigations on cells with ferroelectric liquid crystalline materials
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In cells with a ferroelectric liquid crystalline polymer the following effects have been observed: Distributions symmetrical to the middle of the cell with opposite orientation of the polarization vector at both surfaces of the LCP layer due to surface interaction have been found by cooling the sample from its isotropic phase to room temperature without application of a field. Switching between two states with opposite orientation of the polarization vector and uniform distribution over the cell was observed by short time application of an electric field above the glass transition. These states can be frozen in by subsequent cooling below the glass transition of the material and are long time stable at room temperature.

articleTitle: Effect of dipolar arrays on the localization of charge carriers in molecular materials
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Recent decades have seen a revival of the interest in studies of the transport and localization of charge carriers in molecular solids, stimulated by several current and emerging applications of these materials. Of particular interest to the matter of this paper is the situation when a molecular system consisting of nonpolar molecules is doped with polar guest species. In this case, permanent dipole moment of the dopant molecules modifies locally the polarization energy, the changes resulting in the appearance of local states in the vicinity of the dopant. Earlier calculations of the author demonstrated that the presence of dipoles in non-polar molecular lattices may result in creation of traps as deep as several tenths of an electronvolt. While the earlier papers considered the effect of isolated dipoles (thus reflecting the situation in nearly-perfect molecular crystals), this contribution will report on results of similar calculations performed on systems mimicking molecularly doped polymers and molecular glasses in which the concentration of dopants is so high that the dipoles cannot be treated as isolated.

articleTitle: Thermal ageing of P(VDF/TrFE) film [for transducers]
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: It was reported by many authors that the properties of P(VDF/TrFE) polymer can be tailored by matching the, conditions of heat treatment to the requirements of various devices. We were interested in designing both the impedance and resonance frequency of P(VDF/TrFE) film for combined and coupled transducers. It is not easy to select a complementary transmitter-receiver pair of identical resonance frequencies, and in general, the frequency of the couple is located on the slope of the resonance characteristics of the both transducers. This is energetically inconvenient and frequency matching of the transmitter-receiver pair is poor or even the pair should be cast away. Results of our studies show that by proper heat treatment of P(VDF/TrFE) film one can easily match the resonance frequencies of coupled transducers and reduce the amplifier system.

articleTitle: On the compensation law observed in thermally stimulated current experiments
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: We have outlined a possible explanation for the observed compensation law in TSDC experiments. The existence ofa current peak in TSDC implies a relationship between the adimensionalised activation enthalpy and entropy. Thus, when the activation entropy of a relaxation process increases the enthalpy will also increase necessarily in order that the peak temperature remains more or less in the same region.

articleTitle: On the electrical and dielectric properties of Nylon 11
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The electrical and dielectric properties of ferroelectric Nylon 11 have been studied using alternating current (AC), thermally stimulated depolarization current (TSDC), direct current (DC) for a triangular signal with a very low period, and isothermal discharging current measurements. Measurements were carried out in a broad temperature range from -170 to 200/spl deg/C. The primary /spl alpha/ relaxation associated with the glass transition and two secondary relaxations were observed. In order to analyze the influence of water on the relaxation spectrum, the AC measurements have been carried out on dry, normal and humid samples, in the frequency range from 10 MHz to 1 MHz. Water increases the strength of secondary /spl beta/ relaxation and shifts the peaks to lower temperatures/higher frequencies. The agreement between the electrical conductivity of the material determined from DC and AC measurements is good and the activation energy of the conductivity is 1.4 eV.

articleTitle: The polarization phenomena in /spl alpha/-PbO photoelectret ceramic
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The most important of the chemical compounds of lead are the lead oxides. Lead oxides are technologically important because they exhibit obvious photoactivity over a wide range of wavelengths; it is for this reason that they are used in imaging devices, particularly, in production of television pickup tubes of "Plumbicon" type, electrophotographic plates, and ferromagnetic and ferroelectric materials. Complex crystal structures, unusual polymorphic transformations, as well as nonstoichiometric forms of lead monoxide have attracted the efforts of many researchers for almost half of a century. The stoichiometry of lead oxides was a subject of early investigations and a large number of research papers published by this time, where matters were considered related to methods employed when preparing and studying any possible oxides and homogeneous phases that are intermediate in composition interval from red lead Pb/sub 3/O/sub 4/ up to lead dioxide PbO/sub 2/. Subject of this study are the polarization properties in the tetragonal lead monoxide. The crystallographic features of structure also are considered. Significant influence of the Pb/sup 2+/ electron lone pairs in the area of low temperature phase transitions is supposed to take place.

articleTitle: Low-frequency dielectric spectroscopy of polymer dielectric films
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The paper presents results of investigating the frequency dependence of a.c. conductivity of non-polar (PTFE) and polar (PVDF) polymers. The picture of charge transport in polymer dielectric films is worked out.

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated current study of crystalline benzene derivatives-trichloro- and dichloromethylbenzenes
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Thermally stimulated current (TSPC and TSDC) have been measured with the pressed discs of 1,2,4-tr-chlorotrimethyIbenzene (1,2,4-TCTMB), 1,8-dichlorotetramethybenzene (1,3-DCTMB) and 1,2-dichlorotetramethylbenzene (1,2-DCTMB) between liquid nitrogen temperature and /spl sim/10/spl deg/C. These materials show a single broad peak that is tailing in the higher temperature range of peak. The peak temperature of these derivatives Tm at which maximum current occurred was found always at -137/spl deg/C, -145/spl deg/ and -154/spl deg/C, respectively, under various polarizing conditions with the constant heating rate 2.5/spl deg/C/min. The peak shape was broad compared with pentachlorotoluene, due to the mutual interaction of adjacent methyl groups. The polarization mechanism of these was discussed in relation with the crystal data.

articleTitle: Thickness and roughness measurements in poly(o-methoxyaniline) layer-by-layer films using AFM
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) was employed to monitor the buildup of layer-by-layer films of poly(o-methoxyaniline) (POMA) and poly(ethenesulfonic acid) (PVS) onto several substrates. Using the contact mode of an AFM, we produced a furrow on the film, which was made possible because the film material was less stiff than the substrate and the silicon tip. Film thickness could then be measured using the tapping mode. The thickness and adsorbed amount of POMA/PVS increased linearly after several bilayers had been deposited, while the roughness increased with the number of bilayers until reaching a saturation value. This behavior was attributed to the ability of these polymers to aggregate, which was confirmed by an analysis of grain sizes.

articleTitle: Spontaneous depolarization current in different mole ratio VDF/TrFE ferroelectric copolymers
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Vinylidene fluoride (VDF)/trifluoroethylene (TrFE) ferroelectric copolymer samples with different mole ratio of 56/44, 70/30 and 77/23 were fabricated by casting from methyl ethyl ketone and followed by slowly cooling from the melting state. Trapped delocalized charges during circulating thermo-stimulating have been observed as spontaneous depolarization current (SDC). For the VDF(56)/TrFE(44) copolymer, SDC spectra show a positive current peak at 72/spl deg/C during heating and a negative peak at 58/spl deg/C during cooling. For the VDF(70)/TrFE(30) copolymer, SDC spectra display a positive current peak at 114/spl deg/C during heating and present a negative peak at 58/spl deg/C and a positive one at 52/spl deg/C during cooling, respectively. As for the VDF(77)/TrFE(23) sample, SDC show a negative peak at 71/spl deg/C and a positive one at 63/spl deg/C during cooling. By comparison with DSC measurements, the peaks are ascribed to the conformation change during ferro-to-paraelectric or para-to-ferroelectric phase transition in heating or cooling processes. This is also an evidence of two coexistent ferroelectric phases in the VDF/TrFE copolymers.

articleTitle: Broadband dielectric spectroscopy on ferrofluids in an external magnetic field
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Temperature dependent dielectric spectroscopy data of magnetic fluids are presented. Under an applied magnetic field, the inner topology of the samples and thus their dielectric properties change. The first results provide evidence for the formation of chain-like structures, in agreement with small-angle X-ray scattering and computer simulations.

articleTitle: Interferometric and surface plasmon modulation in glass polymer hybrid waveguides
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Hybrid photonic devices based on evanescent field interaction are realized with linear and Mach-Zehnder interferometer structures in passive glass waveguides by arrangement of a polymer-metal layer system as active cover.

articleTitle: The behavior and state of mixed Langmuir monolayer at air-water interface
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The Langmuir-Blodgett (LB) technology is an excellent method for the preparation of ultrathin films with a controlled thickness and well-defined molecular order. The materials of choice for constructing the LB films cover a wide range from low molecular weight amphiphiles to performed polymers and biological compounds. At the same time, with the combination of materials science and life science, it is more important and valuable to study the structure of LB films made by protein and lipid and their relation. Then in order to obtain good biological LB films, available film-forming conditions must be obtained. Therefore, it is important and essential to study the behavior and states of bovine serum albumin-phosphatidylcholine (BSA-PC) monolayer at air-water interface. The target of using BSA-PC is to form a measure of preparing biological molecular LB films so that we can simulate biological environment and make further investigation on interactive mechanism and application of biological molecular films. It is also important to further study on bionics. The investigation of the change of behavior of BSA-PC mixed monolayer at air-water interface is the subject of this paper.

articleTitle: Preparation and properties of CuPc/ZnO hybrid composite films
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Nitric dioxide (NO/sub 2/) is one kind of toxic gas in the atmosphere which does great harm to the environment and the health of humans. So, it is very important to obtain the concentration of NO/sub 2/ in the environment timely and accurately, so as to monitor and protect the environment. Because of the high sensitivity and high selectivity of phthalocyanine (Pc), it has been widely studied. Here, a novel kind of CuPc/ZnO hybrid composite gas-sensitive film prepared by vacuum evaporation is studied. The results show that CuPc/ZnO hybrid composite films have good gas-sensitivity to NO/sub 2/, good selectivity and short response time. The resistivity decreases 3-4 order of magnitude compared with pure CuPc film. At the same time, the sensitivity mechanism of CuPc/ZnO hybrid composite films and the influential factors are primarily studied.

articleTitle: Numeric reconstruction of a distribution of electrically active defects in PVDF from the thermoluminescence spectra
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In the thermally stimulated luminescence spectrum of PVDF three peaks are found in the temperature range 120 K (/spl gamma/-peak), 190 K (/spl beta/-peak) and 320 K (/spl alpha/-peak). The use of numeric methods for experimental results development with the application of the regularization algorithms of Tikhonov (1986) and the method of varying the sample heating rate, allows one to define in a reliable way the parameters of the most probable activation energy and the effective frequency factor of electrically active defects for all relaxation processes in PVDF.

articleTitle: Dielectric and photochemical behavior of amorphous copolymers containing photochromic azobenzene side groups
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: A combination of optical spectroscopy with real time dielectric spectroscopy is used to investigate the structural changes and the dynamics induced by the E/Z-isomerization of azobenzene moieties in photochromic polymers.

articleTitle: Optical constants and dielectric permittivity of lutetium oxide films deposited with an electron gun
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Lu/sub 2/O/sub 3/ films deposited by electron-beam evaporation exhibit interesting optical properties in the range 0.2 - 2 /spl mu/m. The films exhibit very good transparency over a wide spectral range. Only a very small influence of the deposition pressure as well as thermal annealing of specimens on optical properties was observed. Refractive index and its dispersion over a wide spectral region was determined. Films exhibit only a weak absorption in violet and ultraviolet ranges. The high-frequency dielectric permittivity was estimated. Thin films of LU/sub 2/O/sub 3/ can be useful for thin-film optics. Lu/sub 2/O/sub 3/-Si antireflection coatings were fabricated. These coatings reduce reflectivity of silicon-based photocells from 35% at /spl lambda/=0.56 /spl mu/m down to 0.9%.

articleTitle: Coordination compounds with insulating and anticorrosive properties
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The present paper is a continuation of our studies regarding the synthesis and the properties of some new coordination compounds obtained by the interaction of the "d" block elements acetylacetonates or acetates with diorganophosphinic acids. Its aim is to determine the influence of the metallic cations and of the ligands on the dielectric properties of the obtained coordination polymers. Taking into account that these compounds also presented good anticorrosive properties, we will try to put some stress on their possible practical applications.

articleTitle: TSDC study of relaxations in drawn semi-crystalline polyesters containing a rigid amorphous fraction
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The influence of the crystalline phase on the /spl alpha/ and /spl beta/-relaxations in thermoplastic polyesters is studied in this paper and the validity of the three phases model is discussed. The TSDC data of various semi-crystalline poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) is compared with the TSDC data of poly(ethylene glycol-co-cyclohexane-1,4-dimethanol terephthalate) (PETG) which is an amorphous copolyester based on PET and PCT.

articleTitle: Analysis of polarization and space charge in thermally poled PVDF
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The spatial distribution of the space charge (SC) and polarization in thermally poled polyvinylidenefluoride (PVDF) can be studied using laser intensity modulation method (LIMM). The actual amount of charge existing in the poled specimen can be determined by hysteresis and thermally stimulated discharge current (TSDC) measurements. The hysteresis measurements are directly sensitive to polarization while the other method is sensitive to both the polarization and SC. PVDF is a ferroelectric polymer which contains polar crystals in which the direction of polarization can be reversed by an application of an appropriate electric field. It is interesting to try to determine the contribution of polarization charge and space charge to observed effects. Present work reports the results concerning the magnitude and spatial distribution of polarization/space charge in PVDF, determined from hysteresis, TSDC and LIMM measurements.

articleTitle: Study of the relaxation process in a side-chain copolymer functionalized with the nonlinear optical chromophore DR13
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: A side-chain copolymer of methylmethacrylate and a methacrylate functionalized with the nonlinear optical, NLO, chromophore 4-[N-ethyl-N-(2hydroxyethyl)]-2'-[chloro-4-nitroazobenzene], DR13, was investigated. The isothermal decay of the electro-optic coefficient, r/sub 13/, was fitted with the Kohlraush-Williams-Watts, KWW, stretched exponential allowing temperature, T/sub G/, to be determined. Above T/sub G/, /spl tau/ was obtained from dielectric loss measurements also using the KWW equation. It was concluded that such relaxation, associated with the chromophore, follows the a relaxation of the copolymer. Its dependence on temperature has the Arrhenius behavior below T/sub G/ and the Vogel-Fulcher-Tammann (VFT) behavior above T/sub G/. An attempt was also made to investigate the applicability of the Dissado-Hill model to account for the r/sub 13/ decay.

articleTitle: Fractal property of some insects' electric charge
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The experiment illustrates that the property of insect electric charge is a fractal characteristic, that is to say, the mass of insects and electric charge brought by themselves have a fractal regularity. With the increase of mass of insects, the insect electric charge in static status is non-linear but fractal to the mass. The value of the fractal dimension E is 1.08409.

articleTitle: Coordination polymers of the 3d block cations with semiconductor properties
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: This work continues the study of the compounds synthesized by the interaction between the acetylacetonates of 3d cations (Sc(IIl), Ti(IV), V(III), Cr(III), Mn(II), Fe(III), Co(II), Ni(II), Cu(II) and ZN(II)) with diphenylphosphinic, diphenyltiophosphinic and diphenylditiophosphinic acids. The aim of the paper is to correlate the structure with their properties, especially with the electric ones, focusing on the influence of the sulfur atoms from the coordinating groups.

articleTitle: Polarization phenomena in blends of polyurethane and styrene-acrylonitrile
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Dielectric measurements, by means of thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC), ramp voltage and reverse I-V characteristics, were used to study molecular mobility and polarization phenomena in blends of thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) and styrene-acrylonitrile copolymer (SAN) with different SAN contents. We observed a plasticization action of SAN content on secondary /spl gamma/, /spl beta/ and primary /spl alpha/ relaxation of TPU rich phase of the blends. The heterocharge relaxation observed in the high temperature region of TSDC thermograms shifts to lower temperatures with increasing TPU content in the blends. From reverse I-V characteristics we calculated the carrier mobility, which was found to follow Arrhenius behavior, as well as the activation energy of the mechanism.

articleTitle: Photoinduced discharge of SiO/sub 2/ electret films. I. Experimental results
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The charge stability in thermally grown silicon dioxide layers during irradiation with monochromatic ultraviolet light has been investigated. The samples were prepared by thermal oxidation of the Si wafer at 1000/spl deg/C and charged by a constant-voltage corona method. A Xenon arc lamp in combination with a monochromator was used to generate monoenergetic photons. The surface potential was measured in dependence on the photon energy, the irradiation intensity, and the charge polarity. During an irradiation period of several hours, the surface potential of negatively charged samples remained constant. In contrast, positively charged samples showed a charge decay which was accelerated by a reduction of the light wavelength as well as an increase of the radiation intensity. A theoretical model for the interpretation of the experimental data is presented in the second part of this contribution.

articleTitle: Dielectric relaxation spectroscopy in polymers: broadband ac-spectroscopy and its compatibility with TSDC
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Dielectric spectroscopy provides information on molecular dynamics and free charge carriers. While a direct characterization of homogeneous material is possible, the permittivity of blends and mixtures also reflects the microstructure. Intrinsic parameters, such as relaxation time and relaxation strength of a polar component, are only obtained via an effective medium analysis. The superposition of independent relaxation processes can be analyzed in terms of 2-dimensional distributions of relaxation times and activation energies. Dielectric relaxation spectroscopy (DRS) and the measurement of thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC) allow an independent evaluation and test of distribution functions.

articleTitle: Determination of polarisation profiles in P(VDF-TrFE) films with LIMM and LITP
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Vinylidenefluoride-trifluorethylene copolymer films were polarized under different conditions and then investigated with the laser intensity modulation method (LIMM) and the laser induced thermal pulse technique, (LITP). For thick films with thick electrodes the results derived from LIMM and LITP experiments are identical. For thin films experimental and methodical constraints influence the applicability and resolution achieved with LITP.

articleTitle: Detrapping behavior of trapped space charges in ferroelectric copolymers of vinylidene fluoride with trifluoroethylene
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Three kinds of slowly-cooled ferroelectric VDF/TrFE copolymer samples with different VDF contents (56, 70, 77 mole%) were prepared by casting from methyl ethyl ketone solution and followed by cooling slowly from melting state to room temperature. The thermally stimulated depolarization current (TSDC) of the copolymer has been measured at various polarization temperatures (60-130/spl deg/C). In the TSDC spectra, three peaks of detrapping charges for VDF(70)/TrFE(30) and VDF(77)/TrFE(23), two peaks for VDF(56)/TrFE(44) are observed. According to the peaks appeared at different cooling temperature during polarization and the analysis of phase transition, the structural origin of the TSDC peaks is proposed. The detrapping density of trapped charges shows that the ability of charge storage for VDF(70)/TrFE(30) is higher than that for other two copolymers.

articleTitle: Cold crystallization effects in PET and PEN by TSDC, DSC and X-ray diffraction
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: A comparative study of the different relaxations present in amorphous and partially crystallized poly(ethylene-2,6-naphthalene dicarboxylate) (PEN) and poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) has been carried out by thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and X ray diffraction. Amorphous films have been crystallized thermically at temperatures between 170/spl deg/C and 200/spl deg/C (PEN); 100/spl deg/C and 150/spl deg/C (PET) by the thermal stimulation by steps method (TSS). DSC measurements of these samples show the appearance of a small endothermic prefusion peak once the crystallization of the sample is completed. This peak increases and shifts towards higher temperatures as the sample is further thermally treated. Associated with the appearance of this endothermic peak, the /spl rho/ relaxation passes through a maximum with a sharp decrease with further heat treatment. X-ray diffraction measurements of these samples show that the decrease in the /spl rho/ peak is associated to the improvement of the amorphous-crystal interphases. This can explain as well the endothermic peak that appears by DSC.

articleTitle: Thermal depolarization studies of hydrophilic sites in polycrystalline siliceous sandstone
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: We study the dielectric properties of polycrystalline sandstone with inherent humidity, by employing the thermal depolarization (thermally stimulated depolarization current, TSDC) spectroscopy. We employ the advantageous selectivity of the TSDC scheme to identify and characterize different hydrophilic sites in sandstone.

articleTitle: Characterization of thermoplastic apparent interpenetrating polymer networks CPU-S/AA by WAXS, SAXS, TSDC, DRS and DMA
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Thermoplastic apparent interpenetrating polymer networks (t-AIPNs), prepared by mechanical blending in a common solvent of crystallisable polyurethane (CPU) and styrene/acrylic acid random copolymer (S/IAA), were investigated by means of wide-angle and small-angle X-ray scattering (WAXS and SAXS), thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC) measurements in the temperature range 77-420 K, dielectric relaxation spectroscopy (DRS) measurements in the frequency range 10/sup -2/-10/sup 6/ Hz and dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) measurements in the frequency range 10/sup -1/-10/sup 2/ Hz and the temperature range 180-500 K. Several mechanical and dielectric relaxations were observed and analysed. The two components show weak affinity to each other. The t-AIPNs can be classified into two groups with high and low contents of CPU, showing essentially the behaviour of CPU and of S/AA, respectively. On the other hand, deviations from additivity in several properties indicate interactions between the two components, caused by the formation of H-bonds between their functional groups, and resulting in partial miscibility. In addition, significant changes are observed on some properties of the t-AIPNs on addition of small amounts of either of the components.

articleTitle: Efficient data conversion in time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In applications of time-domain dielectric spectroscopy, in which frequency-domain information is obtained by means of Fourier transformation of step-response data, results are often required at a number M of evenly spaced frequencies, where M is considered smaller than N, the number of equidistant samples from which the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) is formed. The object of this paper is to point out a method for reducing the computing effort required by fast Fourier transformation (FFT) techniques used for collecting spectral data.

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated depolarisation currents in model epoxy networks: experimental evidence for local and non-local relaxation processes
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: We have shown in a recent publication, (Henn et al, J. Appl. Phys. vol.85, p.2821, 1999), that it is possible to distinguish between local and non-local, i.e. collective processes of dielectric relaxation measured in various classes of solids. This discrimination is made feasible by varying the heating rate of the thermally stimulated depolarisation currents (TSDC) and by measuring the evolution of the shape of the glow curve. If the thermally stimulated dielectric response arises from a distribution of relaxation times, then the width of the glow curve increases with increasing heating rate, On the other hand, in the case of a polymeric material, the TSDC signals obtained in the Tg region exhibit an opposite heating rate dependence: the width of the glow curve is a decreasing function of the heating rate. This behaviour has been explained as being the result of non-local relaxation processes. The aim of the present work is to show that these findings can be generalised to other types of polymeric materials, in which a progressive change from local to non-local relaxation modes is observed. For this purpose, we selected a series of epoxy networks, based on the diepoxide DGEBA and aliphatic amines, and whose sub-Tg relaxational behaviour has already been identified as involving both isolated and short-scale cooperative molecular motions.

articleTitle: Dielectric behaviour of polycarbonate/poly(styrene-co-acrylonitrile) blends
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In this work we investigate the dielectric behaviour of blends of polycarbonate/poly(styrene-co-acrylonitrile) (PC/SAN) in a broad frequency and temperature region. Main attention is devoted to the effect of miscibility and interphase interactions on the shape and position of dielectric functions in dependence on temperature and frequency.

articleTitle: Some aspects concerning dielectric behaviour of copper containing magnetic ceramics
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Since the polycrystalline ferrites are very good dielectric materials, the dielectric constant /spl epsiv//sub /spl tau// and the loss tangent tg/spl delta/ in copper-zinc, copper-nickel and copper-manganese ferrites has been studied as a function of composition, frequency and temperature. Interesting results were obtained concerning the dependence of the dielectric parameters on frequency and temperature. We have found that in these ferrites the Cu/sup +/ ions which appear during the sintering process by reduction of Cu/sup 2+/ ions have a great influence upon the dielectric properties. As a result of the presence of Cu/sup 2+/ ions, the copper containing ferrites show a p-type electric conduction. This fact determines an abnormal behaviour of the dielectric parameters as a function of frequency and temperature.

articleTitle: The influence of environment on discharging currents in polyethylene terephthalate
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In order to understand the nature of the origin of the released current in the temperature range from room temperature up to 220 /spl deg/C, TSDC and the isothermally final discharging current (IFDC) have been measured, in vacuum and in different ambient gases for PET specimens. The behavior of the samples polarized in oxygen, in nitrogen and in ambient air was analyzed. The contribution of the heterocharge, the homocharge and the absorbed gases to the measured current is analyzed.

articleTitle: Polar intramolecular salts N-(indan-1,3 dion-2-yl) pyridinium betaine derivatives. Their electronic properties
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In this work, in order to study the influence of heteroatoms and different functional groups in molecules on the electronic properties, a wide class of IPB derivatives is chosen. The experimental data on the electronic structure of thin evaporated films of IPB and its eleven derivatives are described.

articleTitle: Influence of impurities on the TSDC signal obtained for unsaturated polyester resins
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The origins of the peaks observed in thermally stimulated depolarized current (TSDC) spectra obtained with unsaturated polyester resins (UPRs) with different amounts of promoter were investigated. It was possible to observe both the classical noncooperative /spl beta/ relaxation peak and the /spl alpha/ peak (the dielectric manifestation of the glass transition). This peak is overlapped with a third one, called /spl rho/, of very great magnitude, located a few degrees above the /spl alpha/ peak. With the help of X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy investigations, we have shown that the promoter of the UPR contains many impurities. Using systems with different amounts of promoter, we have shown that the origin of the /spl rho/ peak can be directly linked to the presence of these impurities.

articleTitle: New electrode materials with modified properties
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: This work presents a new method and the suitable installation of obtaining electrode materials with modified properties, necessary for the electrodes used especially in some industrial electrochemical processes. The modification of electrode material characteristics intends to obtain some electrocatalytical properties and also, high stability of electrode potential in time. Other purposes of these modifications are: the increment of corrosion resistance in aggressive mediums, especially under polarisation conditions in acid or chloride solutions, and the improvement of the active layer adhesion on the electrode surface. The proposed method is in accordance with the mentioned purposes and also eliminates the disadvantages caused by other methods, as the oxides dispersion in the flame of the combustion gases in order to obtain active oxide layer on the metallic surface. It consists in depositing, by electrical discharge, of successive oxide layers on an electrode surface (usually, a metallic surface). The nature and the proportion of the used oxides depend on the electrode destination (e.g. electrocatalytical properties, stability and corrosion resistance, etc.).

articleTitle: Charge transport, adsorption and percolation transitions on electrified surface
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In the present work the surface discharge of electrets is considered. Particular attention is given to the phenomena of adsorption and nucleation of electrically conducting phase in the course of percolation charge transport on the electrified surface. The basis for consideration is formed by the percolation model of charge relaxation in electrets originally proposed in 1984. This model is founded on the simultaneous use of percolation theory and Kolmogorov conception for 2D nucleation kinetics. Such an approach has allowed to get a quantitative description for charge decay on the electrified surface under the action of electrically conducting external agent, primarily, the ambient air humidity.

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated polarization and depolarization currents in molybdenum doped PbWO/sub 4/ single crystals
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Thermally stimulated polarization and depolarization current technique was used to monitor (in the temperature range of 100/spl divide/450 K) the dielectric relaxation of Czochralski's-grown PbWO/sub 4/ single crystals containing different amount of Molybdenum. It has been found that the TSDC-spectrum of these crystals consists of two bands the position (T/sub m/) and amplitude (H/sub m/) of which is sensitive to the presence of the dopant and the atmosphere of both thermal treatment of samples and the experiments performed.

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental analysis of electron beam irradiated polymers
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Charge transport and storage phenomena were analyzed in Teflon FEP, polyethylene (PE), and poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) foils irradiated with partially penetrating electron beams, in a Split Faraday Cup (SFC) arrangement. Measurements of electrical current were performed during the electron irradiation. The irradiated front electrode was grounded while the rear electrode was positively biased. The experimental results were fitted by models which considered two different media: the irradiated region (I) and the non-irradiated one (NI). In the later, NI-region, the intrinsic electrical properties of the material were considered. In the I-region, on the other hand, effects of irradiation, as carrier generation, recombination effect and trapping-detrapping phenomenon play a fundamental role in the transport process. Beside the explanation of the experimental behavior observed in each material, the theoretical treatment provided important electrical parameters.

articleTitle: Scanning force microscopy investigations on electroactive polymer films
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The authors present investigations on a PVDF (polyvinylidenefluoride) film supplied with top and bottom Au electrodes, which is analysed using a SFM and a contactless optical sensor to measure the sample strain with respect to applied fields.

articleTitle: Molecular mobility and hydration properties in polyurethane and styrene-acrylonitrile blends
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: Dielectric measurements by means of thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC) techniques in the temperature range 90-300 K were used to study molecular mobility and morphology in blends of polyurethanes based on branched polymer polyol (PUR) and styrene-acrylonitrile copolymer (SAN) with different SAN content. Water sorption/desorption isotherms both in equilibrium (ESI) and dynamic (DSI) were used to measure isothermal water uptake and diffusion coefficients. Water sorption has a significant influence on the /spl gamma/ and /spl beta/ relaxations. With increasing water content the MWS peak shifts to lower temperatures. For all samples studied the amount of water at saturation was found to decrease with increasing temperature and SAN content in the blends.

articleTitle: Physicochemical and dielectric study of the hydration mechanism in polysaccharides
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In this work, the hydration mechanism of soluble starch has been investigated by means of equilibrium water sorption and desorption isotherms, and of thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC) techniques in the temperature range 77-300 K. The water content, h, of the samples was varied between 0 and 0.39 g of water/g of dry sample. The results of equilibrium water sorption measurements were analyzed by means of the Guggenheim-Anderson-De Boer (GAB) equation in terms of bound and clustered water. Two TSDC peaks were observed and the dependence of their characteristics on water content was studied.

articleTitle: Information regarding the structure of new complex oxide based on Ca, Cd, Ri and Nb from dielectric measurements. Aurivillius or pyrochlore?
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: The synthesis of mixed oxides based on Ca, Cd, Bi and Nb made the object of different studies, the obtained materials having, according to the authors, pyrochlore or perovskite structures. The pyrochlore type compounds usually crystallize in the cubic system (space group Fd3m and a=10 A), containing eight molecules per unit cell, while the real perovskite type compounds present distortions to lower symmnetry classes. On the other hand, Rao and Medvedeva pointed out the presence of Aurivillius type structures for the mixed oxides containing Bi, Ca and Nb, The Aurivillius type oxides could be represented as a combination of (Bi/sub 2/O/sub 2/) fluorite type and (A/sub n-1/B/sub n/O/sub 3n-1/ perovskite-like layers, where n is an integer. As we already know, some members of the perovskite and Aurivillius type structures show superconductivity, but not even one compound with pyrochlore structure have been reported to present this phenomenon. On the other hand, due to their structural compatibility, the Aurivillius and perovskite type oxides are suitable to be used as supports for the thin film HTS. Our attempts to synthesise mixed oxides in the pseudo-quaternary system CaO-CdO-Bi/sub 2/O/sub 3/-Nb/sub 2/O/sub 5/ led to a compound having the chemical composition close both to a substituted pyrochlore and to a superior member of an Aurivillius series. In the present work, we will try to elucidate, by means of physicochemical characterization methods, including the dielectric measurements, the membership of the synthesised oxide to one of the above mentioned structures.

articleTitle: Effect of past history on triboelectrification of ice
publicationTitle: 10th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 10). Proceedings (Cat. No.99 CH36256)
abstract: In order to verify the origins of the charging phenomena, an examination of the triboelectrification of pure ice was made using a couple of ice rods with identical properties.
